post_understanding.summary: Wrapping an anti-semi join query in IF EXISTS in SQL Server 2012 causes a plan change that makes it much slower (minutes vs seconds). The EXISTS introduces a row goal, leading the optimizer to choose a nested loops, non-parallel plan instead of a (parallel) hash anti-join.
symptoms: Significant slowdown only when wrapped in IF EXISTS (minutes vs seconds)
Execution plan switches from Hash Match + Parallelism to Nested Loops without parallelism
Higher logical reads and row-by-row lookups into smalltable
Same logical query semantics; only plan shape differs
suspected_root_causes: Row goal introduced by EXISTS leading to nested loops and removal of parallelism
Cardinality/distribution skew causing nested loops to perform many lookups before finding a qualifying row
Parameterization context within stored procedure (parameter sniffing may amplify but not required)
Stats and index choices affecting join strategy preference
key_evidence: Author reports: SELECT completes in ~3 seconds; IF EXISTS version takes ~10 minutes
Answer cites: EXISTS introduces a row goal that favors Nested Loops or Merge Join over Hash Match and removes parallelism
Both queries are the same except EXISTS; execution plans differ (links provided in post)
SQL Server 2012 context with default behavior for row goals
assumptions: SQL Server 2012 instance with default cost threshold for parallelism and MAXDOP settings (assume cost threshold = 5, MAXDOP > 1)
Both tables exist in the same SQL Server instance; cross-database join is permitted (bigtable in somedb, smalltable in current DB)
bigtable is large (tens of millions of rows) with an index on (databasename, source); smalltable has an index/unique key on (source)
For databasename = 'someval', a large number of rows qualify in bigtable, and most of their sources exist in smalltable (anti-semi matches are rare, e.g., ~1–10%)
Data is distributed so that early rows (by the index used to satisfy databasename = 'someval') mostly match smalltable, forcing nested loops to perform many lookups before finding a non-matching row
Auto-create/update statistics is ON and up to date
No significant concurrent workload is required to reproduce the issue

target_tables.purpose: Large fact-like table providing many candidate rows for databasename='someval' to drive plan choice differences between EXISTS and non-EXISTS versions.

columns.name: source
columns.role: join/anti-join key to smalltable; also used in filter source <> 'kt'

columns.name: payload
columns.role: row bloat to mimic real table width and IO patterns

generated_data_plan.distribution: databasename values: 'someval' for 20% (~10M rows), remainder spread across ~100 other names; source values: ~5,000,000 distinct overall with skew such that for databasename='someval' most sources appear in smalltable and only ~5% do not; arrange insertion so early index order for (databasename, source) favors sources present in smalltable, with non-present sources clustered toward the end.
generated_data_plan.rationale: Large outer input with many qualifying rows ensures nested loops will perform many lookups under a row goal before finding a qualifying anti-semi row; supports hash anti-semi join and parallelism in the non-EXISTS version.

target_tables.purpose: Lookup/reference table joined on source for anti-semi logic.

generated_data_plan.distribution: Contains ~95% of the ~5,000,000 distinct source values used by bigtable for databasename='someval'; missing ~5% chosen to be greater values by collation so they sort after present ones when scanning index (to delay first anti-semi hit).
generated_data_plan.rationale: Large reference set enables a fast hash anti-join for the non-EXISTS version and many successful probes for the EXISTS nested loops before finding a non-existing source.

anomaly_injection.name: baseline_non_exists_select
anomaly_injection.method: Execute the non-EXISTS SELECT that returns the qualifying rows, capturing plan and metrics.

parameters.sql: SELECT l.databasename FROM somedb.dbo.bigtable AS l WHERE l.databasename = N'someval' AND l.source <> N'kt' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.smalltable AS c WHERE c.source = l.source);
parameters.expected_plan_shape: Parallel Hash Match (anti-semi) with a scan/seek on bigtable filtered by databasename='someval' and a hash build on smalltable(source)

safety_notes: Large scans may consume CPU/IO; monitor and cap MAXDOP if needed

anomaly_injection.name: exists_row_goal_injection
anomaly_injection.method: Wrap the same logic in IF EXISTS to introduce a row goal and force a different optimization path.

parameters.sql: IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM somedb.dbo.bigtable AS l WHERE l.databasename = N'someval' AND l.source <> N'kt' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.smalltable AS c WHERE c.source = l.source)) BEGIN; RAISERROR('Source missing', 16, 1); RETURN; END;
parameters.expected_plan_shape: Non-parallel Nested Loops (anti-semi) probing smalltable for each qualifying bigtable row under a row goal
parameters.session_settings: Use default MAXDOP and cost threshold; ensure AUTO UPDATE STATISTICS is ON

safety_notes: Query may run for minutes due to row-by-row probes; be prepared to cancel if resource contention occurs
Confirm indexes and statistics are in place to avoid confounding missing-index issues

anomaly_injection.name: mitigation_hash_join_hint_check
anomaly_injection.method: Apply a HASH JOIN hint within the IF EXISTS to validate that the slowdown is due to the row goal causing nested loops.

parameters.sql: IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM somedb.dbo.bigtable AS l WITH (INDEX(IX_bigtable_databasename_source)) INNER HASH JOIN dbo.smalltable AS c ON c.source = l.source WHERE l.databasename = N'someval' AND l.source <> N'kt' AND c.source IS NULL) BEGIN; RAISERROR('Source missing', 16, 1); RETURN; END; -- Alternatively: IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM somedb.dbo.bigtable AS l WHERE l.databasename = N'someval' AND l.source <> N'kt' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.smalltable AS c WHERE c.source = l.source)) OPTION (HASH JOIN);
parameters.expected_plan_shape: Hash anti-join (may still be non-parallel due to IF EXISTS, but significantly faster than nested loops)

safety_notes: Hints are for diagnostic confirmation only; remove for true reproduction of the anomaly
Ensure hinted plan compiles successfully; adjust index names as implemented

metrics.expected_change: IF EXISTS version increases by >10x compared to baseline SELECT
increase due to many outer probes with nested loops
significant increase due to many key lookups/probes
drops to 1 for IF EXISTS plan; baseline uses >1 if server allows
baseline shows Hash Match (anti-semi) + Parallelism; IF EXISTS shows Nested Loops (Left Anti Semi Join) with Row Goal property

query_or_transaction_effects: Baseline SELECT returns the anti-semi rowset in seconds
IF EXISTS version does not return rowset but completes far slower before RAISERROR/RETURN
Hinted or rewritten IF EXISTS (LEFT JOIN/EXCEPT or OPTION(HASH JOIN)) performs closer to baseline
validation_criteria: Observe IF EXISTS plan containing a Nested Loops anti-semi join and single-threaded execution (or otherwise measurably slower)
Observe baseline SELECT plan containing a Hash Match anti-semi join with parallelism
Timing difference consistent with the post (seconds vs minutes) on the generated data
When applying a HASH JOIN hint or rewriting to LEFT JOIN/EXCEPT inside IF EXISTS, performance improves and plan shape aligns with hash anti-join
